abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is an opportunistic pathogen that causes various diseases in animals and humans. Small RNAs (sRNAs) control major steps in the infection process and acclimation responses, contributing to the architecture of the regulatory networks. However, a large number of putative sRNAs remain poorly characterized. Here we present aureoRNA, an interactive database (https://aurorna.biologie.uni-freiburg.de) that integrates available information for each sRNA, including phylogeny in the phylum Bacillota, public transcriptome datasets for sRNA and mRNA correlation, and permits computational predictions of sRNA functions. The aureoRNA-based analysis of the sRNA RsaD revealed new targets including the oxidative threonine catabolism and the arginine deiminase pathway. A target-centric search identifying potential sRNAs for mRNAs of interest revealed the citZ citrate synthase mRNA as an RsaE target, and two small prophage genes as RNAIII interaction partner. The aureoRNA database facilitates the functional characterization of the entire set of sRNAs and their targets in this major pathogen.
